1. Code generators: Code generators are tools that automatically generate code based on a set of rules or templates. They can be used to automate code generation for specific programming languages or frameworks. Some popular code generators include ANTLR, ProGuard, and Yeoman.

Benefits:

* Reduces development time and effort
* Consistency in code style and structure
* Can be used to generate boilerplate code

Trade-offs:

* Limited to specific programming languages or frameworks
* May not be able to handle complex or custom code
* May require some manual configuration and customization

Example: ANTLR is a popular code generator that can be used to generate code for parsing and analyzing programming languages. It uses a grammar-based approach to generate code that can be customized for specific use cases.

1. Template engines: Template engines are tools that allow you to define templates for generating code. They can be used to generate code for a variety of programming languages and frameworks. Some popular template engines include Mustache, Handlebars, and EJS.

Benefits:

* Flexible and customizable templates
* Can be used to generate code for multiple programming languages and frameworks
* Can handle complex or custom code

Trade-offs:

* May require some manual configuration and customization
* Can be more complex to set up and maintain

Example: Handlebars is a popular template engine that can be used to generate HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code. It allows you to define templates that can be customized for specific use cases.

1. Machine learning algorithms: Machine learning algorithms can be used to generate code automatically based on patterns and relationships in code repositories. They can be used to generate code for a variety of programming languages and frameworks. Some popular machine learning frameworks include TensorFlow and PyTorch.

Benefits:

* Can handle complex or custom code
* Can learn from large code repositories
* Can generate code that is optimized for specific use cases

Trade-offs:

* Requires a large amount of training data
* May require some manual configuration and customization
* Can be more complex to set up and maintain

Example: TensorFlow can be used to train machine learning models that can generate code for specific programming tasks, such as code completion or bug detection. These models can be customized for specific use cases and can learn from large code repositories.

In summary, code generators, template engines, and machine learning algorithms are all approaches that can be used to automate code generation. Each approach has its own benefits and trade-offs, and the best approach will depend on the specific use case and requirements.

context: Ten European football teams – the Netherlands, England, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and Wales – will participate in a season-long “OneLove” campaign promoting inclusion and opposing discrimination.
expected_response:
Every country except Sweden and Norway has qualified for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and each captain of these eight nations will wear a distinctive OneLove armband – which features a heart containing colors from all backgrounds – during the tournament.
The Netherlands FA, which is spearheading the campaign, chose the colors to represent all heritages, backgrounds, genders and sexual identities; the armband will be worn in Qatar where same-sex relationships are a criminal offense.
Sweden and Norway will participate in the initiative during the upcoming Nations League matches, while England will also wear black armbands during both its UEFA Nations League matches to mark the death of Queen Elizabeth II.
“This is an important message which suits the game of football: on the field everybody is equal and this should be the case in every place in society. With the OneLove band we express this message,” said Virgil van Dijk, the Netherlands captain.
“On behalf of the Dutch team I have been wearing this band for quite a while now. It is good to see that other countries are joining this initiative.”
OneLove was founded in the Netherlands in 2020 to emphasize that all football fans have at least one thing in common – their love of football – and to speak out against any form of discrimination.
As well as focusing on public messaging, the initiative has also developed to offer diversity training to grassroots club.
“Our love of football unites us all. No matter where you come from, what you look like and who you love. Football is there for everyone and our sport must stand up for the people across the world who face discrimination and exclusion,” said Germany captain Manuel Neuer.
“I am proud to be sending out this message with my colleagues from the other national teams. Every single voice counts.”
In June, England’s captain Harry Kane revealed that he had discussed taking a collective stance regarding human rights in Qatar with Denmark’s Christian Eriksen and France captain Hugo Lloris.
“I am honored to join my fellow national team captains in supporting the important OneLove campaign,” he said on Tuesday.
“As captains we may all be competing against each other on the pitch, but we stand together against all forms of discrimination. This is even more relevant at a time when division is common in society. Wearing the armband together on behalf of our teams will send a clear message when the world is watching.”

Job: Software Engineer

Receive and perform code reviews with other engineers.
Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests to verify functionality using automated testing frameworks such as Pytest.
Work collaboratively with fellow software engineers to build features requested by business stakeholders.
Participate in Agile teams to develop, test, and debug complex data processing pipelines and data analysis applications using big data processing systems such as Apache Spark.
Diagnose, debug, and perform root cause analysis of issues and defects.
Skills and experience that will lead to success:
Experience with a modern software programming language. We use Python, and Pyspark extensively.
Experience with cloud systems like AWS or Azure
Experience writing SQL queries 
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Eagerness to work in a highly-collaborative environment
Some visualization experience such as Tableau or PowerBI is helpful

Software Engineer

1. The Importance of a Strong Brand Identity

A strong brand identity is crucial for the success of any business. It sets you apart from your competitors, helps you build a loyal customer base, and contributes to your overall brand recognition. In this section, we'll explore the key elements of a strong brand identity and how to create one that resonates with your target audience.

1.1 The Key Elements of a Strong Brand Identity

A strong brand identity is built on a combination of visual and verbal elements. These include:

* Logo: A well-designed logo is the cornerstone of your brand identity. It should be memorable, unique, and easily recognizable.
* Color Palette: Choose colors that reflect your brand personality and appeal to your target audience.
* Typography: Select fonts that are legible, consistent, and reflect your brand's personality.
* Tagline: A catchy tagline can help reinforce your brand's message and make it more memorable.
* Brand Voice: Establish a consistent tone and style for your brand's messaging, including your website, social media, and marketing materials.

1.2 Creating a Strong Brand Identity

To create a strong brand identity, follow these steps:

* Conduct market research to understand your target audience and competitors.
* Define your brand's unique value proposition and personality.
* Develop a brand style guide that outlines your visual and verbal elements.
* Consistently apply your brand identity across all marketing channels.
* Monitor and evolve your brand identity as your business grows and changes.

1.3 The Benefits of a Strong Brand Identity

A strong brand identity offers numerous benefits, including:

* Increased brand recognition and awareness.
* Improved customer loyalty and retention.
* Better differentiation from competitors.
* Higher perceived value and prestige.
* Easier marketing and advertising efforts.

By investing in a strong brand identity, you'll set your business up for long-term success and help it stand out in a crowded marketplace.

1. The Importance of Mental Health in the Workplace

Mental health is a critical aspect of overall well-being, and it plays a significant role in the workplace. Mental health issues can affect an individual's ability to perform their job duties, and it can also impact the productivity and morale of the workplace. In this section, we will discuss the importance of mental health in the workplace and how it can affect individuals and organizations.

Firstly, mental health issues can affect an individual's ability to perform their job duties. For example, an employee with depression may struggle to focus, make decisions, and communicate effectively, which can negatively impact their job performance. Similarly, an employee with anxiety may experience difficulty in social situations, which can affect their ability to work effectively in a team. Therefore, it is essential for employers to recognize the signs of mental health issues in their employees and provide support to help them manage their mental health.

Secondly, mental health issues can impact the productivity and morale of the workplace. For example, an employee with depression may take more sick days, which can affect the productivity of the organization. Similarly, an employee with anxiety may experience difficulty in communicating with colleagues, which can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts, affecting the morale of the workplace. Therefore, it is essential for employers to create a supportive work environment that promotes mental health and well-being.

Thirdly, mental health issues can have legal implications for employers. For example, employers have a legal obligation to provide a safe and healthy workplace, which includes promoting mental health and well-being. Failure to do so can result in legal action, fines, and negative publicity. Therefore, it is essential for employers to comply with legal requirements related to mental health in the workplace.

In conclusion, mental health is an essential aspect of overall well-being, and it plays a significant role in the workplace. Employers have a legal obligation to provide a safe and healthy workplace, which includes promoting mental health and well-being. By recognizing the signs of mental health issues in their employees, creating a supportive work environment, and complying with legal requirements, employers can promote mental health and well-being in the workplace, which can lead to improved job performance, productivity, and morale.

1. Introduction

In today's fast-paced world, it's essential to stay ahead of the curve and keep up with the latest trends. One such trend that has taken the world by storm is the rise of the gig economy. The gig economy refers to a labor market characterized by the prevalence of short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs. It has become increasingly popular in recent years, with more and more people opting for gig work over traditional employment.

1.1 The Gig Economy: A Brief Overview

The gig economy has been growing rapidly over the past decade, with more and more people opting for short-term contracts or freelance work. According to a report by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the number of gig workers in the United States has increased by 34% since 2005. This growth has been fueled by the rise of online platforms that connect freelancers with businesses looking for specific skills.

1.2 The Benefits of the Gig Economy

The gig economy offers a number of benefits to both workers and businesses. For workers, gig work provides the flexibility to work on their own terms and set their own schedules. It also allows them to work on a project-by-project basis, which can lead to greater job satisfaction and a more diverse range of experiences.

For businesses, the gig economy provides access to a wider pool of talent, as they can hire freelancers with specific skills or expertise that may not be available in-house. It also allows them to scale up or down quickly, depending on their needs.

1.3 The Challenges of the Gig Economy

While the gig economy offers many benefits, it also comes with its fair share of challenges. One of the biggest challenges is the lack of job security. Freelancers are not entitled to the same benefits as traditional employees, such as health insurance or retirement plans. This can make it difficult for freelancers to plan for the future and can also lead to financial instability.

Another challenge is the lack of social protections. Freelancers are not entitled to the same protections as traditional employees, such as unemployment benefits or workers' compensation. This can make it difficult for freelancers to access support in the event of illness or injury.

1.4 The Future of the Gig Economy

Despite the challenges, the gig economy is here to stay. In fact, many experts predict that it will continue to grow in the coming years. As technology advances and more businesses shift towards remote work, the gig economy is likely to become an even more significant part of the labor market.

1.5 Conclusion

In conclusion, the gig economy has become an increasingly popular option for workers and businesses alike. While it comes with its fair share of challenges, it also offers a number of benefits that make it an attractive option for many. As the gig economy continues to grow, it will be important for both workers and businesses to understand the implications of this trend and how to navigate its challenges.

These powerful tools have the potential to revolutionize the way businesses operate, from automating routine tasks to providing valuable insights that drive decision-making.

1. The Role of AI and ML in Business

AI and ML technologies have become increasingly important in the business world, offering a range of benefits that can help companies stay ahead of the competition. Some of the key ways these technologies are being used in business include:

* Automating routine tasks: AI and ML can be used to automate repetitive and time-consuming tasks, freeing up employees to focus on more strategic work.
* Improving decision-making: By analyzing large amounts of data, AI and ML can provide valuable insights that can inform decision-making and help companies make more informed choices.
* Enhancing customer experiences: By using AI and ML to personalize customer interactions and provide more tailored experiences, businesses can improve customer satisfaction and loyalty.
* Streamlining operations: AI and ML can be used to optimize processes and workflows, reducing inefficiencies and improving overall productivity.
1. The Benefits of AI and ML in Business

The benefits of using AI and ML in business are numerous, and include:

* Increased efficiency: By automating routine tasks and optimizing processes, AI and ML can help businesses operate more efficiently and effectively.
* Improved decision-making: By providing valuable insights and data-driven recommendations, AI and ML can help businesses make more informed decisions.
* Enhanced customer experiences: By using AI and ML to personalize customer interactions and provide more tailored experiences, businesses can improve customer satisfaction and loyalty.
* Competitive advantage: By leveraging AI and ML technologies, businesses can gain a competitive edge and stay ahead of the competition.
1. The Risks of AI and ML in Business

While AI and ML offer many benefits, there are also some risks and challenges that businesses need to be aware of. Some of the key risks include:

* Bias and discrimination: If not properly addressed, AI and ML systems can perpetuate biases and discrimination, leading to unfair outcomes.
* Data privacy and security: AI and ML rely on large amounts of data, and businesses need to ensure that this data is collected and used in a secure and ethical manner.
* Ethical considerations: There are ethical considerations that need to be taken into account when using AI and ML, including issues related to transparency, accountability, and human oversight.

In conclusion, AI and ML technologies have the potential to revolutionize the way businesses operate, offering a range of benefits that can help companies stay ahead of the competition. However, it is important for businesses to be aware of the risks and challenges associated with these technologies, and to take steps to address them. By doing so, businesses can leverage the power of AI and ML to drive growth, improve efficiency, and enhance customer experiences, while also ensuring that they are operating in a responsible and ethical manner.

ori_prompt: Write a step-by-step guide for resolving GitHub merge conflicts.
expected_response:
1- Under your repository name, click Pull requests.
2- In the "Pull Requests" list, click the pull request with a merge conflict that you'd like to resolve.
3- Near the bottom of your pull request, click Resolve conflicts.
4- Decide if you want to keep only your branch's changes, keep only the other branch's changes, or make a brand new change, which may incorporate changes from both branches. Delete the conflict markers <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>> and make the changes you want in the final merge.
5- If you have more than one merge conflict in your file, scroll down to the next set of conflict markers and repeat steps four and five to resolve your merge conflict.
6- Once you've resolved all the conflicts in the file, click Mark as resolved.
7- If you have more than one file with a conflict, select the next file you want to edit on the left side of the page under "conflicting files" and repeat steps four through seven until you've resolved all of your pull request's merge conflicts.
8- Once you've resolved all your merge conflicts, click Commit merge. This merges the entire base branch into your head branch.
9- If prompted, review the branch that you are committing to.
If the head branch is the default branch of the repository, you can choose either to update this branch with the changes you made to resolve the conflict, or to create a new branch and use this as the head branch of the pull request.
If you choose to create a new branch, enter a name for the branch.
If the head branch of your pull request is protected you must create a new branch. You won't get the option to update the protected branch.
Click Create branch and update my pull request or I understand, continue updating BRANCH. The button text corresponds to the action you are performing.
10- To merge your pull request, click Merge pull request. For more information about other pull request merge options, see "Merging a pull request."

* Open the GitHub repository and navigate to the branch you want to merge.
* Check the file(s) that have a merge conflict. You should see a message indicating that there is a conflict in the file(s).
2. Open the conflicting file(s):
* Click on the file(s) that have a merge conflict. This will open the file(s) in your code editor.
3. Resolve the conflict manually:
* Look at the conflicting changes and decide which changes to keep and which to discard. You can do this by comparing the changes side-by-side or by using a diff tool.
* Once you have decided which changes to keep, edit the file to remove the conflicting changes.
* Save your changes and close the file.
4. Commit the changes:
* Go back to the command line or code editor and navigate to the parent directory of the conflicting file(s).
* Run the command `git add <file(s)>` to add the changes you made to the conflicting file(s) to the staging area.
* Run the command `git commit -m "Resolved merge conflict in <file(s)>"` to commit the changes with a commit message that describes the conflict and the resolution.
5. Push the changes:
* Run the command `git push` to push the changes to the remote repository.
6. Check the conflict resolution:
* Go back to the GitHub repository and check that the conflict has been resolved. You should see that the file(s) no longer have a merge conflict message.
* Verify that the changes have been pushed to the remote repository.

Note: If you are unable to resolve the conflict manually, you may need to contact the repository owner or seek help from a team member. Additionally, be sure to carefully review any changes made to the code during the conflict resolution process to ensure that the code is functioning correctly and that there are no unintended side effects.

bpo_response:
以下是一个示例 GitHub Actions workflow 文件，它演示了如何自动执行代码检查、构建、测试和部署：
```yaml
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Set up JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v2
        with:
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Build and test
        run: ./gradlew build && ./gradlew test
      - name: Deploy to staging
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
        with:
          name: Staging
          path: dist
```
这个 workflow 的名称是 `CI/CD`，它将在主分支上的推送事件和拉取代码事件触发。它包含一个名为 `build-and-test` 的作业，该作业将在 Ubuntu 最新版本上运行，并包括以下步骤：

1. 从代码仓库中获取代码。
2. 设置 JDK 17。
3. 构建和测试代码。
4. 将测试结果上传到存储库中。

在构建和测试步骤中，`./gradlew build` 和 `./gradlew test` 命令分别执行构建和测试。最后，`./gradlew test` 命令将测试结果上传到名为 `Staging` 的存储库中，该存储库位于作业的工作目录中。

这个 workflow 可以通过在 GitHub 上创建一个 YAML 文件来定义，并将其与项目关联。当某个事件发生时，GitHub Actions 将自动执行该 workflow 中的作业。

1. Create a new file in the repository called `.github/workflows/example.yml`
2. Define the workflow in the file as follows:
```
name: Example Workflow

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Run tests
      run: |
        npm install
        npm test
```
3. This workflow will run whenever a commit is pushed to the `main` branch, and will run the `build` job on an Ubuntu machine. The job will run two steps: it will check out the code using the `actions/checkout` action, and then it will run the `npm install` and `npm test` commands to install and test the code.
4. To schedule the workflow to run on a certain schedule, you can use the `cron` job scheduler. For example, to run the workflow every day at 8am, you can add the following line to the `build` job:

name: CI/CD Workflow

首先，在 GitHub 倉庫的 `.github/workflows` 目錄中創建一個名為 `deploy-to-production` 的工作流程文件。
```yaml
name: Deploy to Production

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v2

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v2
      with:
        node-version: 14

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm install

    - name: Build and package
      run: npm run build

    - name: Deploy to production
      run: npm run deploy
```
這個工作流程會在主分支的 `push` 事件發生時自動執行。它包含兩個作業：`build` 和 `deploy`。

`build` 作業使用 `actions/setup-node` 步驟來安裝 Node.js 14，然後使用 `npm install` 來安裝依賴項。接下來，使用 `npm run build` 來編譯並打包應用程序。

`deploy` 作業則使用 `npm run deploy` 來執行部署的指令，例如使用 `cap` 來部署 Node.js 應用程序。

除了自動執行，這個工作流程還可以透過手動啟動或安排的方式執行。例如，可以使用 `curl` 或 `wget` 下載並執行 `deploy-to-production.yml` 檔案，或者使用 GitHub Actions UI 來手動啟動作業。

1. The Great Barrier Reef, Australia

The Great Barrier Reef is a living masterpiece, a natural wonder that deserves to be visited by everyone. It is the world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 kilometers along the coast of Australia. It is home to an incredible diversity of marine life, including over 1,500 species of fish, 600 types of soft and hard corals, and various other creatures such as dolphins, turtles, and whales.

One of the unique aspects of the Great Barrier Reef is its sheer size and complexity. It is made up of thousands of individual coral reefs and hundreds of islands, cays, and coral cays. Visitors can explore the reef by snorkeling, diving, or taking a boat tour, and discover a world of vibrant colors, exotic fish, and fascinating coral formations.

Another attraction of the Great Barrier Reef is its rich history. The reef has been inhabited by indigenous Australian communities for thousands of years, and European explorers began to visit the area in the 16th century. Today, the reef is protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is a popular destination for eco-tourism.

The Great Barrier Reef is also significant for its environmental importance. It is one of the most biodiverse ecosystems on the planet, providing a vital habitat for countless species and playing a crucial role in the global carbon cycle. However, the reef is under threat from climate change, pollution, and other human activities, making it all the more important for visitors to learn about and appreciate its unique beauty and importance.

In conclusion, the Great Barrier Reef is a truly remarkable place that deserves to be visited for its natural beauty, cultural significance, and environmental importance. Whether you're a seasoned diver or just looking for a unique travel experience, the Great Barrier Reef is an unforgettable destination that will leave you with memories to last a lifetime.

A static website is a website whose content does not change unless the website owner manually updates it. The content of a static website is pre-built and stored on the server, and the web browser retrieves the static content from the server each time the website is accessed. Static websites are typically faster and more affordable to create and maintain than dynamic websites.

On the other hand, a dynamic website is a website whose content is generated by a web application or a database. The content of a dynamic website is generated on the fly each time the website is accessed, based on user input or other factors. Dynamic websites are typically more complex and expensive to create and maintain than static websites, as they require a web application or a database to generate the content.

1. Algorithms and Data Structures: This topic is important because it is a fundamental aspect of computer science. Employers want to know that you have a strong understanding of common algorithms and data structures, and can apply them to solve problems efficiently.
2. Object-Oriented Programming: This topic is important because it is a fundamental aspect of modern programming. Employers want to know that you have a strong understanding of object-oriented concepts, such as encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism, and can use them to write clean, maintainable code.
3. Programming Languages: This topic is important because it shows your proficiency in a specific programming language. Employers want to know that you are comfortable using a particular language and can write code in it effectively.
4. Databases: This topic is important because it shows your understanding of how data is stored and retrieved in a computer system. Employers want to know that you can design and implement databases, and can use SQL to query and manipulate data.
5. Operating Systems: This topic is important because it shows your understanding of how computer systems work. Employers want to know that you can design and implement operating systems, and can troubleshoot common issues.
6. Networking: This topic is important because it shows your understanding of how computer systems communicate with each other. Employers want to know that you can design and implement network protocols, and can troubleshoot common issues.
7. Security: This topic is important because it shows your understanding of how to protect computer systems from unauthorized access. Employers want to know that you can design and implement secure systems, and can identify and mitigate common security threats.
8. Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC): This topic is important because it shows your understanding of how to develop software effectively. Employers want to know that you can follow a structured process to develop software, and can identify and mitigate common issues that arise during the development process.

1. Fundamentals of computer science:
	* History of computing and its evolution
	* Basic concepts of computer hardware and software
	* Operating systems and their functions
	* Networking and communication protocols
	* Data representation and manipulation
2. Programming languages:
	* Common programming languages (e.g., C, C++, Java, Python, JavaScript)
	* Language features and syntax
	* Data types, variables, and operators
	* Control structures (e.g., loops, conditional statements)
	* Functions and modules
	* Object-oriented programming (OOP) concepts
	* Design patterns and best practices
3. Data structures and algorithms:
	* Arrays, linked lists, stacks, and queues
	* Trees (binary, AVL, B-trees)
	* Graphs (directed, undirected)
	* Hashing and hash tables
	* Sorting and searching algorithms (e.g., quicksort, mergesort, heapsort)
	* Dynamic programming and memoization
	* Time and space complexity analysis
4. Software engineering:
	* Software development life cycle (SDLC) models (e.g., Waterfall, Agile, Scrum)
	* Requirements gathering and analysis
	* Design patterns and principles (e.g., SOLID, DRY)
	* Test-driven development (TDD) and unit testing
	* Version control systems (e.g., Git, SVN)
	* Project management and estimation techniques
	* Code reviews and continuous integration
	* Deployment and cloud computing
5. Advanced topics:
	* Machine learning and artificial intelligence
	* Data mining and knowledge discovery
	* Natural language processing
	* Computer vision and image processing
	* Distributed systems and concurrency
	* Security and cryptography
	* Database systems and data warehousing
	* Human-computer interaction and user experience design

ori_prompt: You will need to guide this person through the scenario they have described for the interview.
context:
Finally! After a while of shooting in the dark and frantically fiddling with sample inputs on the whiteboard, you've came up with an algorithm for solving the coding question your interviewer gave you.
Whew. Such a relief to have a clear path forward. To not be flailing anymore.
Now you're cruising, getting ready to code up your solution.
When suddenly, your interviewer throws you a curve ball.
"What if we thought of the problem this way?"
You feel a tension we've all felt during the coding interview:
"Try to listen to what they're saying...but don't lose your train of thought...ugh, I can't do both!"
expected_response:
Your interviewer probably won't fault you for going down the wrong path at first. They've seen really smart engineers do the same thing. They understand it's because you only have a partial view of the maze.
They might have let you go down the wrong path for a bit to see if you could keep your thinking organized without help. But now they want to rush you through the part where you discover the dead end and double back. Not because they don't believe you can manage it yourself. But because they want to make sure you have enough time to finish the question.
But here's something they will fault you for: failing to listen to them. Nobody wants to work with an engineer who doesn't listen.
So when you find yourself in that crucial coding interview moment, when you're torn between holding your train of thought and considering the idea your interviewer is suggesting...remember this:
Listening to your interviewer is the most important thing.
Take what they're saying and run with it. Think of the next steps that follow from what they're saying.
Even if it means completely leaving behind the path you were on. Trust the route your interviewer is pointing you down.
Because they can see the whole maze.

context:
Mathematics and art are related in a variety of ways. Mathematics has itself been described as an art motivated by beauty. Mathematics can be discerned in arts such as music, dance, painting, architecture, sculpture, and textiles. This article focuses, however, on mathematics in the visual arts.
Mathematics and art have a long historical relationship. Artists have used mathematics since the 4th century BC when the Greek sculptor Polykleitos wrote his Canon, prescribing proportions conjectured to have been based on the ratio 1:√2 for the ideal male nude. Persistent popular claims have been made for the use of the golden ratio in ancient art and architecture, without reliable evidence. In the Italian Renaissance, Luca Pacioli wrote the influential treatise De divina proportione (1509), illustrated with woodcuts by Leonardo da Vinci, on the use of the golden ratio in art. Another Italian painter, Piero della Francesca, developed Euclid's ideas on perspective in treatises such as De Prospectiva Pingendi, and in his paintings. The engraver Albrecht Dürer made many references to mathematics in his work Melencolia I. In modern times, the graphic artist M. C. Escher made intensive use of tessellation and hyperbolic geometry, with the help of the mathematician H. S. M. Coxeter, while the De Stijl movement led by Theo van Doesburg and Piet Mondrian explicitly embraced geometrical forms. Mathematics has inspired textile arts such as quilting, knitting, cross-stitch, crochet, embroidery, weaving, Turkish and other carpet-making, as well as kilim. In Islamic art, symmetries are evident in forms as varied as Persian girih and Moroccan zellige tilework, Mughal jali pierced stone screens, and widespread muqarnas vaulting.

1. The Importance of Emotional Intelligence in the Workplace

a. Definition and Explanation of Emotional Intelligence

Emotional intelligence (EI) refers to the ability to recognize, understand, and manage one's own emotions, as well as the emotions of others. It encompasses a range of skills, including self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, and social skills. EI is essential in the workplace because it helps individuals navigate complex interpersonal dynamics, communicate effectively, and build strong relationships with colleagues and clients.

b. The Impact of Emotional Intelligence on Workplace Performance

Research has shown that individuals with high emotional intelligence tend to perform better in their jobs and have better workplace relationships. They are more effective in handling conflicts, adapting to change, and leading teams. For example, a study by Daniel Goleman found that employees with high EI are more likely to be promoted, have better job satisfaction, and experience less burnout.

c. Strategies for Developing Emotional Intelligence

To develop emotional intelligence, individuals can start by becoming more self-aware, which involves recognizing and understanding their own emotions and how they impact their behavior. They can also practice self-regulation, which involves managing their emotions in a healthy and productive way. Other strategies include practicing empathy, cultivating strong social skills, and seeking feedback from colleagues and supervisors.

d. Examples of Emotional Intelligence in Action

One example of emotional intelligence in action is a manager who is able to recognize when an employee is struggling with a personal issue and offers support and resources to help them through a difficult time. Another example is a team leader who is able to navigate a conflict between team members by listening to both sides and finding a solution that meets everyone's needs.

e. The Role of Emotional Intelligence in Leadership

Emotional intelligence is particularly important for leaders, who must be able to inspire and motivate their teams, manage change, and navigate complex interpersonal dynamics. Research has shown that emotionally intelligent leaders are more effective in these areas and are more likely to have high-performing teams.

f. The Benefits of Developing Emotional Intelligence

Developing emotional intelligence can have a range of benefits for individuals and organizations, including improved workplace relationships, better job performance, and increased job satisfaction. It can also lead to greater resilience in the face of challenges and a more positive work environment overall.

g. Tips for Improving Emotional Intelligence

To improve emotional intelligence, individuals can start by identifying their own emotional triggers and practicing self-reflection to understand why they react the way they do. They can also seek feedback from colleagues and supervisors and work on developing their social skills, such as active listening and empathy.

h. The Relationship Between Emotional Intelligence and Burnout

Research has shown that individuals with high emotional intelligence are less likely to experience burnout, which is a state of emotional, physical, and mental exhaustion caused by excessive and prolonged stress. By developing their emotional intelligence, individuals can better manage stress and maintain a healthy work-life balance, which can help prevent burnout.

i. The Importance of Emotional Intelligence in the Workplace

Overall, emotional intelligence is a critical skill for success in the workplace. By developing their emotional intelligence, individuals can improve their workplace relationships, communicate more effectively, and perform better in their jobs. Employers can also benefit from promoting emotional intelligence by creating a more positive and productive work environment.

By establishing a robust data governance framework, organizations can leverage their data assets to support their digital initiatives, such as data-driven decision-making, predictive analytics, and machine learning.

Regulatory compliance is essential for organizations that handle sensitive data, such as personal information or financial data, as non-compliance can result in significant fines and reputational damage. Organizations must ensure that they have the necessary policies and procedures in place to maintain compliance with regulatory requirements, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Data privacy and security are critical components of data governance in the digital age. With the increasing volume and variety of data, organizations must ensure that they have the necessary measures in place to protect their data assets from unauthorized access, theft, or loss. This enables organizations to make informed decisions based on data-driven insights, which can help them to improve their operations, reduce costs, and drive innovation.

expected_response:
- Chapter One - Why we Program?
These are the course-wide materials as well as the first part of Chapter One where we explore what it means to write programs. We finish Chapter One and have the quiz and first assignment in the third week of the class. Throughout the course you may want to come back and look at these materials. This section should not take you an entire week.
- Installing and Using Python
In this module you will set things up so you can write Python programs. Not all activities in this module are required for this class so please read the "Using Python in this Class" material for details.
- Chapter One: Why We Program (continued)
In the first chapter we try to cover the "big picture" of programming so you get a "table of contents" of the rest of the book. Don't worry if not everything makes perfect sense the first time you hear it. This chapter is quite broad and you would benefit from reading the chapter in the book in addition to watching the lectures to help it all sink in. You might want to come back and re-watch these lectures after you have funished a few more chapters.
- Chapter Two: Variables and Expressions
In this chapter we cover how a program uses the computer's memory to store, retrieve and calculate information.
- Chapter Three: Conditional Code
In this section we move from sequential code that simply runs one line of code after another to conditional code where some steps are skipped. It is a very simple concept - but it is how computer software makes "choices".
- Chapter Four: Functions
This is a relatively short chapter. We will learn about what functions are and how we can use them. The programs in the first chapters of the book are not large enough to require us to develop functions, but as the book moves into more and more complex programs, functions will be an essential way for us to make sense of our code.
- Chapter Five: Loops and Iteration
Loops and iteration complete our four basic programming patterns. Loops are the way we tell Python to do something over and over. Loops are the way we build programs that stay with a problem until the problem is solved.

ori_prompt: Create a daily itinerary based on the given information.
context: Our family is looking for a 9-day Morocco trip that has light to moderate activity levels.
expected_response:
1- DAY 1: MARRAKECH
Arrive in time to meet your fellow travelers for a welcome gathering this evening. Your arrival transfer is included.
2- DAY 2: MARRAKECH/OUARZAZATE
Wind past red slopes and green terraces as we make our way south through the stunning valleys of Morocco’s High Atlas Mountains, stopping to enjoy a picnic lunch beside a sparkling river. Arrive in Ouarzazate, known as the “gateway to the Sahara,” and step behind the scenes at a film studio to see how the surrounding dunes have starred on the silver screen.
3- DAY 3: OUARZAZATE/MERZOUGA
Today, travel between jagged peaks and palm oases toward the desert town of Merzouga. Settle into our hotel near the incredible Erg Chebbi, a sweeping sea of dunes formed by wind-blown sand. As the sun sets, savour a traditional Amazigh dinner, then spread a blanket on the sand for an evening of desert stargazing.
4- DAY 4: MERZOUGA
This morning, hop aboard a 4x4 and ride across the dunes to discover fossils left behind by an ancient sea, and be entranced by Gnaoua musicians in a local village. Return to the hotel for free time to cool off in the pool. Enjoy a tasty Amazigh dinner, then gather around a glowing bonfire for a storytelling session.
5- DAY 5: MERZOUGA/DADES GORGE
Venture into the rugged landscape of the Dades Gorge, a dramatic and colourful valley carved by the waters of the Dades River. Visit a local village for lunch and enjoy a special dish—traditional Amazigh pizza! Wind through the valley on a guided walk as you learn about the amazing geology behind the weird and wonderful rock formations of the Gorge. This evening, enjoy free time to relax at the hotel.
6- DAY 6: DADES GORGE/AÏT BEN HADDOU
Drive through the Ounila Valley to the ancient fortified village of Aït Ben Haddou, a UNESCO World Heritage site where clay houses crowd together in a traditional ksar behind defensive walls. Explore alleyways twisting between historic structures, and stand guard atop the clay brick ramparts, taking in views of the green oasis around this imposing fort. Entertain your taste buds at a hands-on tagine cooking class, followed by a delicious dinner.
7- DAY 7: AÏT BEN HADDOU/MARRAKECH
Journey through the mountains to Marrakech, known as the “red city” for its walls, houses, and many mosques built from red clay. After checking into your hotel and resting up, head to a local henna workshop to have your hands painted in this ancient temporary tattooing art. Then, explore the lively Djemaa el Fna, an ancient marketplace still used as the main square in Marrakech. After, enjoy free time to discover more of Marrakech.
8- DAY 8: MARRAKECH 
Wake up as the call to prayer echoes across the city. After breakfast, set out on a guided walk through the narrow, maze-like streets of the medina, lined with colorful shops brimming with rugs, spices, and much more. Spend the rest of the day exploring Marrakech on your own, or opt to explore the Marjorelle Garden. In the evening, gather for a farewell dinner in a traditional riad, a grand house with an elegant interior courtyard.
9- DAY 9: MARRAKECH
Depart at any time.

8. Be present: Try to stay in the moment and focus on the task at hand, rather than worrying about what's to come or what's happened in the past.
9. Take breaks: If you're feeling overwhelmed, take a short break to regroup and refocus.
10. Get feedback: Ask for feedback from your teacher or classmates after your presentation to help you improve for future presentations.

What can you make by recycling and repurposing some old, previously used materials? We want to see it!

expected_response:
This power booster recycles a 'dead' battery to power a 1.8 volt red LED light. It's mainly made from recycled parts.
When a 1.5 volt battery is new it will probably have more than 1.5 volts in it. As the battery is used the voltage will decrease until the voltage is not enough to run the application ( E.g. a red LED) and will be called 'dead' . But a Dead battery still has some power remaining in it - just not enough voltage. The trick is to use some of that remaining power to increase the voltage in a circuit. The trade off being there will be a reduction in current.
Here is the required steps:
1- Connect a switch to a battery holder. A soldiering iron and hot glue gun assisted with this.
2- Make a small pyramid above the battery holder using 4 bamboo skewer sticks secured with hot glue.
3- Soldier on a 1.8 volt red LED at the top of the mini Christmas tree.
4- Test the LED glows with a new battery (1.6 volts)
5- Test the LED doesn't glow with a dead battery (1.2 volts)
6- Add in the buzzer circuit, along with a switch.
7- Add in the windings circuit - to touch the striker of the buzzer a little copper foil was added.
8- Insert a dead battery (1.2 volt) with the buzzer circuit turned switch off - the LED will not glow but when the buzzer circuit is switched on the Red LED lights up.

context: Steam Engine Using an Empty Beer Can
expected_response:
Step 1: Close Drink Opening
To build up steam the beverage can needs to act as a pressure vessel and so needs to be completely sealed, except where the steam will come out of the jet nozzles. It also needs to rotate on itself. Bend up the outer tab into a L shape using some pilers and then bend it forward so a piece of string can hang from it over the center of the can. This will allow the can to rotate on itself. Close the pouring opening by using a knife or other thin object, bending the opening back up so it almost where it was before the beverage can was opened.
Step 2: Nozzel Jets
Make a couple of holes in the side of the can, about half way up, opposite each other using a small drill. The diameter of the holes should be about the same as the thin plastic tubing to be used as jet nozzles. Enlarge the holes so they are elliptical allowing the nozzle tubes to lie parallel against the cans side.
Step 3: Making a Pressure Vessel
Seal the top of the opened can using super glue and baking soda to make a small pressure vessel. Add some super glue to the closed opening and then sprinkle on some baking soda - they will combine to make a plastic. Keep adding super glue and baking soda until the top is sealed.
Step 4: Attaching the Nozzle Jets
Fit in the thin plastic tubes to the holes drilled in the sides of the can and seal with super glue and baking soda. Try to have the tubes pointing horizontal in the direction you want to rotate the can when the steam exits the nozzles.
Step 5: Creating Steam
Add a little water into the can though one of the nozzles. Just add maybe a teaspoon or so. 
Step 6: In Action
The can was suspended from a tripod over the methylated sprits flame. After a couple of minutes enough steam had built up to rotate the can.

expected_response: The green light symbolizes several different things to different characters throughout the book, but overall, it stands for the inaccessibility of the American Dream. At the start of the novel, the light symbolizes Gatsby's unwavering love for Daisy. He stands at the end of the dock gazing across the bay, reaching for the light, waiting for Daisy to come back to him. His hope, like the eternal green light, is unfaltering. It isn't until Daisy admits later that she had never really noticed the light that the facade began to slip. Nick, the narrator, starts to recognize it as a symbol of Gatsby's unhealthy desperation rather than his love. This is parallel to Gatsby's experience of the American Dream and money. Gatsby is unbelievably rich at the beginning of the novel. This solidifies his belief in the American Dream, though he still reaches for the acceptance of those who are wealthier and more popular. Nick believes money is not an object to Gatsby, though he has no idea how he made all of it. As the story unfolds and the mystery and mystique around Gatsby fade, so does Gatsby and Nick's blind belief and trust in the American Dream. After Gatsby is murdered, the green light is symbolic of the ways that money and affluence ruin the lives of those without. It is also symbolic of the way that the American dream ruins the lives of those eternally reaching for it.

1. What is the significance of the title "The Tell-Tale Heart" in Edgar Allan Poe's short story?

The title "The Tell-Tale Heart" is significant in Edgar Allan Poe's short story for several reasons. Firstly, it serves as a metaphor for the narrator's guilt and the beating of his heart, which he believes is the cause of the old man's death. The narrator believes that the sound of his own heart is the only evidence of his sanity, but it is also the source of his guilt and the reason for his eventual undoing.

Secondly, the title can be interpreted as a warning to the reader, suggesting that the narrator's actions and the guilt he feels will ultimately lead to his downfall. The phrase "tell-tale" implies that the narrator's guilt will be revealed, and the heart will be the instrument that reveals his true nature.

Finally, the title can also be seen as a commentary on the nature of guilt and the human psyche. The narrator's obsession with his own sanity and the old man's death is driven by his guilt, and the title suggests that the narrator's guilt is a "tell-tale" sign of his true nature.

In summary, the title "The Tell-Tale Heart" is significant in Edgar Allan Poe's short story as a metaphor for the narrator's guilt, a warning to the reader, and a commentary on the nature of guilt and the human psyche.

The title "The Great Gatsby" is significant in several ways. Firstly, it highlights the novel's central character, Jay Gatsby, who is widely regarded as one of the most iconic and enigmatic figures in American literature. The title also suggests that the novel is set in a world of grandeur and excess, where the wealthy elite, such as Gatsby, hold significant power and influence.

1. What is the difference between a traditional IRA and a Roth IRA?

A traditional IRA and a Roth IRA are both types of individual retirement accounts (IRAs) that allow individuals to save for retirement. However, there are some key differences between the two:

1. Contributions: With a traditional IRA, contributions are made with pre-tax dollars, which reduces the taxable income for the year in which the contribution is made. This means that the account holder may be able to deduct the contribution from their taxes. With a Roth IRA, contributions are made with after-tax dollars, meaning that the account holder has already paid taxes on the money contributed.
2. Taxes on withdrawals: With a traditional IRA, withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income. This means that the account holder will have to pay taxes on the money they withdraw from the account at their current tax rate. With a Roth IRA, withdrawals are tax-free, as long as they meet certain requirements.
3. Contribution limits: The contribution limit for a traditional IRA is higher than for a Roth IRA. For the tax year 2023, the contribution limit for a traditional IRA is $6,000, or $7,000 if the account holder is age 50 or older. The contribution limit for a Roth IRA is $6,000, or $7,000 if the account holder is age 50 or older.
4. Eligibility: Anyone who earns income and is under the age of 70 1/2 can contribute to a traditional IRA. With a Roth IRA, eligibility is based on income levels. For the tax year 2023, the income limit for a Roth IRA is $140,000 for single filers and $208,000 for joint filers.

In summary, the main differences between a traditional IRA and a Roth IRA are the way contributions are made, the taxes on withdrawals, the contribution limits, and eligibility. Traditional IRAs are tax-deferred, meaning that contributions are made with pre-tax dollars and withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income. Roth IRAs are taxed upfront, meaning that contributions are made with after-tax dollars and withdrawals are tax-free.

In addition to enhancing the flavor of meats, grilling can also be used to cook vegetables and fruits. When grilled, vegetables and fruits develop a sweet, smoky flavor that is irresistible.

Overall, grilling is a simple yet effective cooking technique that can greatly enhance the flavor profile of a wide variety of foods. Whether you're grilling steaks, vegetables, or fruit, the smoky, caramelized flavor that results is sure to impress.

This allows the meat to cook slowly and evenly, preserving its natural juices and retaining its moisture. The result is a tender, flavorful piece of meat with a consistent texture throughout.

To enhance the flavor profile of the meat, it is important to pair sous vide cooking with the right seasonings and marinades. For example, a dry rub of spices such as garlic, paprika, and cumin can be applied to the meat before vacuum-sealing it in a bag. ori_prompt: Describe how to prepare the given food in your own words. Note down the ingredients you will need and the steps you will take to prepare them.
context: Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
expected_response:
Ingredients (for 12 cookies):
½ cup granulated sugar(100 g)
¾ cup brown sugar(165 g), packed
1 teaspoon salt
½ cup unsalted butter(115 g), melted
1 egg
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 ¼ cups all-purpose flour(155 g)
½ teaspoon baking soda
4 oz milk or semi-sweet chocolate chunks(110 g)
4 oz dark chocolate chunk(110 g), or your preference
Preparation:
In a large bowl, whisk together the sugars, salt, and butter until a paste forms with no lumps.
Whisk in the egg and vanilla, beating until light ribbons fall off the whisk and remain for a short while before falling back into the mixture.
Sift in the flour and baking soda, then fold the mixture with a spatula (Be careful not to overmix, which would cause the gluten in the flour to toughen resulting in cakier cookies).
Fold in the chocolate chunks, then chill the dough for at least 30 minutes. For a more intense toffee-like flavor and deeper color, chill the dough overnight. The longer the dough rests, the more complex its flavor will be.
Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Scoop the dough with an ice-cream scoop onto a parchment paper-lined baking sheet, leaving at least 4 inches (10 cm) of space between cookies and 2 inches (5 cm) of space from the edges of the pan so that the cookies can spread evenly.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges have started to barely brown.
Cool completely before serving.

1. Chicken Tikka Masala:

Ingredients:

* 1 kg boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
* 1 tsp ginger-garlic paste
* 1 tsp ground cumin
* 1 tsp ground coriander
* 1 tsp garam masala
* 1 tsp turmeric
* 1 tsp red chili powder
* 1 tsp amchur (dry mango powder)
* 1 tsp lemon juice
* 1 cup plain yogurt
* 1 cup heavy cream
* 1 cup water
* 1 tsp vegetable oil
* Salt, to taste
* Fresh cilantro, for garnish

Steps:

1. Marinate the chicken pieces in a mixture of yogurt, lemon juice, and spices (ginger-garlic paste, ground cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, turmeric, red chili powder, amchur, and salt) for at least 30 minutes.
2. Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat.
3. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook until they are golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side.
4. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
5. In the same pan, add vegetable oil and heat it over medium heat.
6. Add the onions, garlic, and ginger and sauté until they are lightly browned.
7. Add the marinated chicken back to the pan and stir well.
8. Add the heavy cream and water, and bring the mixture to a boil.
9. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened.
10. Stir in the vegetable oil and remove from heat.
11. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot.

Note: You can adjust the spice level according to your preference by adding more or less of any spice.

* He also discusses the importance of developing a strong faith and a belief in oneself in order to maintain a positive outlook.
* The article concludes with a call to action, encouraging readers to adopt a positive mindset and to share their positive thoughts with others in order to spread positivity and inspire others.

* The article discusses the importance of effective communication in both personal and professional relationships.
* Carnegie emphasizes the importance of listening actively and empathetically, as well as expressing oneself clearly and concisely.
* He also discusses the importance of avoiding criticism and instead focusing on constructive feedback and praise.
* The article concludes with a call to action, encouraging readers to improve their communication skills in order to build stronger relationships and achieve greater success.

* The article discusses the importance of self-discipline in achieving success and personal growth.
* Tracy emphasizes the need to set goals and to take consistent action towards achieving them, even in the face of obstacles and setbacks.
* He also discusses the importance of developing a strong work ethic and of avoiding distractions and procrastination.
* The article concludes with a call to action, encouraging readers to develop their self-discipline in order to achieve their goals and live a fulfilling life.

* The article discusses the importance of persistence in achieving success and overcoming obstacles.
* Hill emphasizes the need to maintain a positive attitude and to keep working towards one's goals, even in the face of setbacks and failures.
* He also discusses the importance of developing a strong willpower and of avoiding negative thoughts and self-doubt.
* The article concludes with a call to action, encouraging readers to develop their persistence in order to achieve their goals and live a fulfilling life.
5. "The Importance of Goal-Setting" by Zig Ziglar
* The article discusses the importance of setting goals in order to achieve success and personal growth.
* Ziglar emphasizes the need to set specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) goals in order to increase the chances of success.
* He also discusses the importance of breaking down larger goals into smaller, more manageable steps and of taking consistent action towards achieving them.

ori_prompt: Give a brief explanation of the requested part of the paper.
context:
Paper: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.

ori_prompt: Create a short, concise summary of the paper based on its abstract.
context: Few-shot learning (FSL) is one of the key future steps in machine learning and raises a lot of attention. In this paper, we focus on the FSL problem of dialogue understanding, which contains two closely related tasks: intent detection and slot filling. Dialogue understanding has been proven to benefit a lot from jointly learning the two sub-tasks. However, such joint learning becomes challenging in the few-shot scenarios: on the one hand, the sparsity of samples greatly magnifies the difficulty of modeling the connection between the two tasks; on the other hand, how to jointly learn multiple tasks in the few-shot setting is still less investigated. In response to this, we introduce FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding. FewJoint provides a new corpus with 59 different dialogue domains from real industrial API and a code platform to ease FSL experiment set-up, which are expected to advance the research of this field. Further, we find that insufficient performance of the few-shot setting often leads to noisy sharing between two sub-task and disturbs joint learning. To tackle this, we guide slot with explicit intent information and propose a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing. Besides, we introduce a Reptile-based meta-learning strategy to achieve better generalization in unseen few-shot domains. In the experiments, the proposed method brings significant improvements on two datasets and achieve new state-of-the-art performance.
expected_response: This paper introduces FewJoint, the first FSL benchmark for joint dialogue understanding, and guides slot with explicit intent information and proposes a novel trust gating mechanism that blocks low-confidence intent information to ensure high quality sharing.

概要：
「幻想の森の秘密」は、若きアーティスト・エマ・ローズと彼女の友人たちが、幻想の森に住む秘密の森の生き物たちと出会い、彼らと共に冒険をする物語です。

キャラクター：

1. エマ・ローズ：主人公のアーティスト・エマ・ローズは、幻想の森に住む秘密の森の生き物たちと出会い、彼らと共に冒険をすることで、自分自身ともに成長し、彼らと共に新しい世界を発見する。
2. シャーロン：エマ・ローズの好きな友人で、彼女と同じように幻想の森に住む秘密の森の生き物たちと出会い、彼らと共に冒険をする。
3. ジェイソン：エマ・ローズの別の好きな友人で、彼女と同じように幻想の森に住む秘密の森の生き物たちと出会い、彼らと共に冒険をする。

設定：
「幻想の森の秘密」は、幻想の森という魔法的な森林の世界で描かれています。この森は、幻想的な生き物たちが住むところで、エマ・ローズと彼女の友人たちが、彼らと共に冒険をすることで、新しい世界を発見する。

コンフリクト：
エマ・ローズと彼女の友人たちは、幻想の森に住む秘密の森の生き物たちと出会い、彼らと共に冒険をすることで、自分自身ともに成長し、彼らと共に新しい世界を発見する。しかし、幻想の森は、幻想的な生き物たちが住むところであり、彼らが暗闇の魔法を使って、エマ・ローズと彼女の友人たちを追い詰めることがある。

エマ・ローズと彼女の友人たちは、幻想の森の生き物たちと共に冒険をすることで、自分自身ともに成長し、彼らと共に新しい世界を発見する。しかし、幻想の森は、幻想的な生き物たちが暗闇の魔法を使って、エマ・ローズと彼女の友人たちを追い詰めることがある。しかし、エマ・ローズと彼女の友人たちは、彼ら自身の力を使って、幻想の森の生

以下是一個可以將複雜度設置為 1 的 bash 指令，它將從一個文本檔中提取所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象，並將它們的 "name" 屬性的值存儲在一個名為 "names" 的陣列中：
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# 讀取文本檔
input_file="input.txt"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    # 提取帶有 "name" 屬性的對象
    if [[ "$line" =~ "name":([^,]+) ]]; then
        name=$BASH_REMATCH[1]
        # 檢查該對象是否已經存在於 names 陣列中
        if [[ -z "$names" ]]; then
            names=($name)
        else
            names=("$names" "$name")
        fi
    fi
done < "$input_file"

# 輸出 names 陣列
echo "$names"
```
這個指令將讀取名為 "input.txt" 的文件，並將每一行中的帶有 "name" 屬性的對象提取出來。如果該對象不是已經存在於 names 陣列中的，則將其添加到 names 陣列中。最後，指令將輸出 names 陣列，這個陣列將包含所有帶有 "name" 屬性的對象。

1. ∀x(P(x) → Q(x))

Translation: For all x, if P(x) is true, then Q(x) must also be true.

Explanation: This sentence is a logical statement that uses the universal quantifier "∀" to indicate that the statement is true for all values of x. The statement asserts that if P(x) is true (meaning that x has the property P), then Q(x) must also be true (meaning that x has the property Q). In other words, if something has the property P, it must also have the property Q.

For example, consider the statement "For all dogs, if the dog is brown, then the dog is happy." This statement is true because it is logically impossible for a dog to be brown and not happy at the same time. The universal quantifier "∀" ensures that the statement is true for all dogs, regardless of their individual characteristics.

Begin near the city of San Diego and make the first stop in coastal La Jolla. This upscale little village is a great a place for an overnight, a day of sunbathing at La Jolla Shores Beach, or a cocktail with a view.
Just 20 minutes north, stop into beachy Encinitas to window shop the boutiques or sample fish tacos. Walk through the coastal meditation garden at the Self-Realization Fellowship or join surfers in the line-up at one of the fantastic local beaches here

As you approach LA, don’t miss swank Laguna Hills. Home to the one-of-a-kind Pageant of the Masters art event, Laguna is brimming with artists and charm. It’s a great place for an overnight. Plus, Crystal Cove Beach in nearby Newport Beach is one of California’s finest!
After that, the choice is yours: Disney lovers should head directly to Disneyland in Anaheim to meet Mickey. To join the beautiful people and snap a photo of an iconic California scene, head to Santa Monica Pier and walk the boardwalk or ride the world’s only solar-powered Ferris wheel. A San Diego to LA road trip is the perfect way to enjoy all things Southern California.

🔹 Project Scope Template for Jira Tickets
===========================================

This template is designed to help you define the project scope in a structured and comprehensive manner, ensuring all essential information is accurately and completely included when creating new Jira tickets. This will facilitate effective issue tracking and management within the Jira system.

### 1. Project Title

* **Project Title**: A brief, descriptive title for the project.

### 2. Project Description

* **Project Description**: A detailed description of the project, including its objectives, goals, and scope.

### 3. Project Goals

* **Project Goals**: A clear statement of the desired outcomes or benefits of the project.

### 4. Scope

* **Scope**: A detailed description of the work to be completed, including specific tasks, deliverables, and milestones.

### 5. Assumptions and Dependencies

* **Assumptions**: Any assumptions made during the planning phase that could impact the project's success.
* **Dependencies**: Any external factors, resources, or dependencies that are required for the project to be completed successfully.

### 6. Stakeholders

* **Stakeholders**: A list of individuals or groups who have a vested interest in the project's success, including project sponsors, team members, and end-users.

### 7. Risks and Mitigation Strategies

* **Risks**: A list of potential risks or challenges that could impact the project's success, along with mitigation strategies to address them.

### 8. Timeline

* **Timeline**: A high-level overview of the project's schedule, including key milestones, deadlines, and dependencies.

### 9. Resources

* **Resources**: A list of the resources required to complete the project, including personnel, equipment, and materials.

### 10. Acceptance Criteria

* **Acceptance Criteria**: A clear set of criteria that must be met for each task or deliverable to be considered complete and accepted by stakeholders.

### 11. Labels

* **Labels**: A list of relevant labels that can be applied to the ticket to help with filtering, prioritization, and organization.

### 12. Attachments

* **Attachments**: Any relevant files, documents, or resources that should be associated with the ticket.

### 13. Comments

* **Comments**: A space for team members to provide additional information, ask questions, or share feedback related to the ticket.

### 14. Status

* **Status**: The current status of the ticket (e.g., open, in progress, completed, blocked, etc.).

### 15. Priority

* **Priority**: The relative importance of the ticket compared to other tasks or issues within the project.

### 16. Sub-Tasks

* **Sub-Tasks**: If applicable, a list of sub-tasks or smaller deliverables that need to be completed as part of the main ticket.

### 17. Epic

* **Epic**: If the ticket is part of a larger, ongoing project or initiative, this field should be used to link the ticket to the relevant epic.

### 18. Task Type

* **Task Type**: The type of task being completed (e.g., bug fix, new feature, documentation, etc.).

### 19. Custom Fields

* **Custom Fields**: Any additional custom fields that are relevant to the project and should be included in the ticket.

### 20. Summary

* **Summary**: A concise summary of the ticket, highlighting its key components and objectives.

By using this template, team members can ensure that all critical aspects of the project scope are accurately and completely included in Jira tickets. This will help to facilitate effective issue tracking and management within the Jira system, ultimately leading to a more successful project outcome.

	* SOA is a design pattern that enables the creation of flexible, modular, and reusable software components.
	* It promotes the development of services that can be easily integrated and composed to create new applications.
2. Components of a Service:
	* Service Name: A unique identifier for the service.
	* Service Description: A brief description of the service's purpose and functionality.
	* Service Interface: The contract between the service and its clients, specifying the operations and data formats that the service supports.
	* Service Implementation: The code that implements the service's behavior and logic.
	* Service Deployment: The process of making the service available to clients.
3. Service Contract:
	* A service contract is a formal agreement between a service provider and its clients.
	* It specifies the terms and conditions under which the service will be provided, including the service's behavior, performance, and security requirements.
4. Service Provider:
	* A service provider is an entity that offers services to clients.
	* It can be a person, organization, or software system that provides services to other entities.
5. Service Consumer:
	* A service consumer is an entity that uses services provided by service providers.
	* It can be a person, organization, or software system that relies on services to perform its functions.
6. Service Registry:
	* A service registry is a database that stores information about available services.
	* It allows service consumers to discover and access services provided by service providers.
7. Service Broker:
	* A service broker is an entity that facilitates the discovery and selection of services by service consumers.
	* It can be a software system that manages the selection and invocation of services based on the service consumer's needs.
8. Service Invocation:
	* Service invocation is the process of requesting a service from a service provider.
	* It involves sending a message to the service provider, specifying the operation to be performed and the data to be passed.
9. Service Orchestration:
	* Service orchestration is the process of coordinating the execution of multiple services to achieve a specific goal.
	* It involves managing the flow of data and control between services to ensure that the overall process is executed correctly.
10. Service Choreography:
* Service choreography is a pattern for composing services to create new functionality.
* It involves defining the interactions between services to achieve a specific goal, without specifying the implementation details of each service.
11. Service Composition:

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
2. In a large mixing bowl, combine 1 lb (450g) of boneless, skinless chicken breasts, 1/2 cup (120ml) of olive oil, 1 tsp (5ml) of dried oregano, 1 tsp (5ml) of dried basil, 1 tsp (5ml) of garlic powder, and 1 tsp (5ml) of salt. Mix well until the chicken is evenly coated with the seasonings.
3. Place the chicken on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).
4. While the chicken is baking, cook 1 cup (200g) of whole wheat pasta according to package instructions.
5. Once the chicken is done, let it rest for a few minutes before slicing it into bite-sized pieces.
6. In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked pasta and sliced chicken.
7. In a small mixing bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup (60ml) of marinara sauce and 2 tbsp (30ml) of grated Parmesan cheese.
8. Pour the marinara sauce and Parmesan cheese mixture over the pasta and chicken mixture and toss until everything is evenly coated.
9. Serve hot and enjoy!

The Australian construction industry is a significant contributor to the country's economy, with the industry generating over $200 billion in revenue in 2020. SMEs in the Australian construction industry face a number of challenges, including access to finance, skilled labor, and technology. 以下是一個簡單的 HTML 範例，用於呼叫一個 JavaScript 函數，並在點擊按鈕時顯示一個彈出框：
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<title>Popup Example</title>
	<script>
		function showPopup() {
			// 在這裡放置你的彈出框內容
			var popup = document.createElement("div");
			popup.innerHTML = "這是一個彈出框";
			document.body.appendChild(popup);
		}
	</script>
</head>
<body>
	<button onclick="showPopup()">點擊這個按鈕</button>
</body>
</html>
```
在這個範例中，我們首先創建了一個名為 `showPopup` 的 JavaScript 函數，該函數會在按鈕被點擊時呼叫。在函數內部，我們使用 `document.createElement` 方法創建了一個新的 `div` 元素，並將其內容設置為 "這是一個彈出框"。然後，我們使用 `document.body.appendChild` 方法將 `div` 元素添加到 `body` 元素中。

接下來，我們在 `body` 元素中添加了一個按鈕，並設置了 `onclick` 屬性，以便在按鈕被點擊時呼叫 `showPopup` 函數。

這樣，當按鈕被點擊時，彈出框就會顯示在網頁上。

1. "The Importance of Emotional Intelligence in the Workplace"

Emotional intelligence (EI) is a critical factor in determining an individual's success in the workplace. It refers to the ability to recognize, understand, and manage one's own emotions, as well as the emotions of others. Research has shown that employees with high emotional intelligence are more likely to have better relationships with their colleagues, communicate more effectively, and be more adaptable to change. They are also more likely to be resilient in the face of challenges and setbacks, and to be able to handle stress and pressure effectively.

Moreover, emotional intelligence is closely linked to leadership skills. Employees with high emotional intelligence are often better equipped to lead teams and make decisions that take into account the needs and feelings of others. They are also more likely to be able to inspire and motivate their colleagues, which can lead to increased productivity and job satisfaction.

In today's fast-paced and ever-changing work environment, emotional intelligence has become an essential skill for success. Employers are increasingly recognizing the value of employees who possess high emotional intelligence and are investing in training and development programs to help their employees improve their EI. By developing their emotional intelligence, employees can not only improve their own performance but also contribute to a more positive and productive workplace culture.

1. "The role of technology in modern society is multifaceted and ever-evolving."

Technology has become an integral part of modern society, transforming the way we live, work, and communicate. From smartphones and social media to artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things, technology has revolutionized virtually every aspect of our lives.

One of the most significant impacts of technology on society is the way it has enabled us to connect with each other on a global scale. Social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram have created virtual communities where people can share their thoughts, ideas, and experiences with each other, regardless of their physical location.

In addition to facilitating communication, technology has also transformed the way we work. With the rise of remote work and telecommuting, employees can now work from anywhere in the world, making it easier to attract and retain top talent. Technology has also enabled businesses to automate many tasks, reducing the need for manual labor and increasing efficiency.

However, the rapid pace of technological advancement has also raised concerns about the potential negative impacts of technology on society. Issues such as privacy violations, cyberbullying, and the potential for job displacement have sparked debates about the ethical implications of technology and the need for regulation.

Overall, the role of technology in modern society is complex and multifaceted, with both positive and negative impacts. As technology continues to evolve, it will be important for society to carefully consider the potential consequences of new technologies and work to ensure that they are used in ways that benefit everyone.

1. "The devil is in the details."

This phrase means that there is often a hidden problem or difficulty lurking in the small, seemingly insignificant details of a situation. It suggests that it's important to pay close attention to the details in order to avoid unexpected problems or difficulties.

For example, imagine that you're planning a big event and you've hired a catering company to provide the food. The caterer promises to provide a certain number of servings of each dish, but when the day of the event arrives, they only bring half the amount of food you were expecting. This could be a problem because you'll have to scramble to find a way to feed all the guests, and it could lead to negative feedback or even legal issues.

In this case, the "devil" is the problem that arises from the small detail of the caterer not providing enough food. By paying attention to the details and ensuring that the caterer's promises are met, you could have avoided this problem and ensured that the event went smoothly.

So, the phrase "the devil is in the details" serves as a reminder to be vigilant and thorough when it comes to the small details of a situation, as they can have a big impact on the outcome.

This phrase means that there is often a hidden problem or issue that is not immediately apparent, but it becomes apparent when you look at the details.

The devil is in the details, and the car is not as good as it seemed at first glance.

In this example, the phrase "the devil is in the details" is used to describe the hidden problem with the car that was not immediately apparent. It is a way of saying that there is often more to a situation than meets the eye, and that it is important to pay attention to the details in order to fully understand the situation.
